steps.content: [Teams Chat] Bagel reports her permissions issue.
The battle ends. Rise takes one last look at Bagel and walks away from the flames.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: After this, Bagel's permissions will be revoked, and their internal security system will soon level up.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Okay, from now on, whether it's a duck or some god developing the game, they'll keep their eye on security loopholes. You won't have to worry about sabotage anymore.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Perfect. Once again, you've done an excellent job.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll take you and everyone else back before they reclaim this power. Let's go now.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Hey, what's the rush? Don't you have something you still want to do?
Rise shoots you a look that says "I know you're trouble," much like when she reported to you at the hospital.
But this time, she keeps quiet, and gets ready to support you.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I'll make sure you get overtime pay. I'll give you quadruple, no, ten times the regular salary, with extra insurance added in.
Next, you look at the icon again.
Look, the entrance to the game is now in your phone. You can check it anytime if you miss home.
In hindsight, this statement is somewhat amusing.
Your world, a city with countless people and memories, fitted into this tiny square... you actually fell for this kind of talk. It really is as fanciful as Mania.
You don't believe anyone can control your world or decide your fate. But if there really is some connection between the two worlds...
Then there's something you must do, and you must do it now.
It's not taking you back to DisCity. The developer permissions you seized from "the gods" are a bit unwieldy, and you barely manage to open a "game entrance."
Beyond the entrance lies a vast space of pure data. Though you don't know the way, you can see a clear trail of abnormal data residues leading deep into the data space.
These are the last tracks she left on her journey, the marks of her struggles.
